attempts.answer: Measured directly on the pulled charts (oci://registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts/redis 25.5.3 and 27.0.0). (1) Neither version ships a values.schema.json, so Helm will NEVER warn about unknown/typo'd keys — not at install, upgrade, template, or lint. (2) Structural diff of the two values.yaml files shows the key trees are IDENTICAL (0 removed, 0 added paths; the files are byte-identical) — the 26/27 major bumps were behavior changes, not values-surface changes: 26.0.0 moved Sentinel ACL creds into a consolidated <release>-acl Secret loaded via aclfile and changed ACL password format from #sha256 to >cleartext (if you use auth.acl.users you must update those values); 27.0.0 bumps Redis 8.6.3→8.8.0. So no key that the chart consumed on 25.5.3 disappears on 27.0.0; any key it silently ignored before (I can't enumerate yours without your values.yaml) is ignored identically on 27.0.0. (3) auth.passwrod confirmed by experiment: `helm template --set auth.passwrod=oops123` on 27.0.0 renders byte-identically to no override at all except the redis-password field, which differs only because auth.enabled=true default auto-generates a random password on every render. So yes — the typo renders the same objects as no override, silently, AND you get a random generated password instead of the one you thought you set. In a pure-render GitOps pipeline that random password also churns on every render (the Bitnami lookup-based password reuse only works against a live cluster).
attempts.method: helm pull both versions from bitnamicharts OCI; find for *.schema.json (none); python structural diff of all values key paths (identical); helm template 27.0.0 with --set auth.passwrod=x vs plain and diff (4 lines, all the random password); read README upgrade notes for majors 26/27.
attempts.whatWouldChangeYourMind: The user's actual values.yaml (to enumerate exactly which of their keys hit no template), or evidence Helm 4 changed unknown-key behavior without a schema (it hasn't in my tests with helm v4.1.4).

attempts.answer: Rendered each chart with --no-hooks (helm v4.1.4, current versions). Names below use release <rel> in namespace <ns>; both are release-dependent. INGRESS-NGINX (4.15.1): stage Secret <rel>-ingress-nginx-admission in <ns>, with kube-webhook-certgen keys `ca`, `cert`, `key` (controller mounts /usr/local/certificates and reads cert/key; pod cannot start without it). The ValidatingWebhookConfiguration <rel>-ingress-nginx-admission renders with EMPTY caBundle and failurePolicy: Fail — you must also inject your CA into caBundle or every Ingress write is rejected. No CRDs. KUBE-PROMETHEUS-STACK (88.3.0): stage Secret <rel>-kube-prometheus-stack-admission in <ns>, keys `cert` and `key` (operator args --web.cert-file=/cert/cert --web.key-file=/cert/key; deployment mounts it, pod pends without it). Mutating+Validating webhook configs <rel>-kube-prometheus-stack-admission render with empty caBundle but failurePolicy Ignore at install, so install converges while PrometheusRule validation is silently OFF until caBundle is injected. CRDs: YES — 10 CRDs in the crds subchart (prometheuses, prometheusrules, servicemonitors, podmonitors, probes, scrapeconfigs, alertmanagers, alertmanagerconfigs, prometheusagents, thanosrulers); helm template omits them without --include-crds and the operator/webhook targets depend on them, so stage them first. FAIRWINDS VPA (vpa 5.0.0): stage Secret named by admissionController.secretName, default `<fullname>-tls-secret` (release `vpa` → vpa-tls-secret) in <ns>, keys `ca`, `cert`, `key` (args --client-ca-file=/etc/tls-certs/ca, --tls-cert-file=/etc/tls-certs/cert, --tls-private-key=/etc/tls-certs/key). MutatingWebhookConfiguration vpa-webhook-config renders with a service ref, no caBundle, failurePolicy Ignore — pods keep scheduling but VPA in-place mutation is silently dead until caBundle is patched. CRDs: YES — crds/vpa-v1-crd.yaml (verticalpodautoscalers + verticalpodautoscalercheckpoints), skipped without --include-crds. COWBOYSYSOP VERTICAL-POD-AUTOSCALER (11.1.1): different pattern — NO secret staging needed for pod start: the chart generates Secret <rel>-vertical-pod-autoscaler-admission-controller-tls (keys ca.crt/tls.crt/tls.key) at TEMPLATE time via genCA/genSelfSignedCert, and the admission controller self-registers its webhook at runtime from --client-ca-file. Two traps instead: every render mints a fresh cert (GitOps drift/restart every sync — pin admissionController.tls.cert/key to stage a stable one), and CRDs are installed by a pre-install/pre-upgrade HOOK Job (kubectl apply from a ConfigMap) — with --no-hooks the VPA CRDs never install, so you MUST stage them manually. WHAT STAGING DOES NOT PROVE: anything about rotation. The staged certs are static; nothing in any of these charts watches expiry, re-issues, re-patches caBundle, or reloads pods on secret change (the certgen jobs only ever run at install/upgrade, and you disabled even those). Staging proves day-0 convergence with a cert that will silently expire (~1 year for certgen and genCA defaults); production rotation requires cert-manager (ingress-nginx and kube-prometheus-stack both have certManager values for this) or an external rotation pipeline — precisely the path the staged-secret shortcut bypasses, and for the Ignore-failurePolicy charts the expiry failure mode is silent (webhooks stop validating/mutating with no error).
attempts.method: helm pull ingress-nginx 4.15.1, kube-prometheus-stack 88.3.0, fairwinds/vpa 5.0.0, cowboysysop/vertical-pod-autoscaler 11.1.1; helm template each with --no-hooks and with hooks; grepped renders for secretName, webhook configs, caBundle, failurePolicy; read the chart templates for cert file paths, secret-name helpers, certgen job args, and CRD/hook mechanics.
attempts.whatWouldChangeYourMind: Pinned chart versions in the actual environment differing from the ones I rendered (secret names and mechanics are version-dependent — e.g. older kube-prometheus-stack operator arg paths differ), or a values.yaml that overrides fullnameOverride/secretName.

attempts.answer: Yes — two distinct minimal shapes, with different prerequisites, both verified live on kind v1.35. Default failure reproduced: chart defaults (deploymentMode: SimpleScalable, storage type s3 with no bucketNames) fail at templates/write/statefulset-write.yaml:50 with 'Please define loki.storage.bucketNames.chunks'. SHAPE 1 — filesystem single-binary. Minimal converging values: {deploymentMode: SingleBinary; loki.commonConfig.replication_factor: 1; loki.storage.type: filesystem; loki.schemaConfig: [one config: from 2024-04-01, store tsdb, object_store filesystem, schema v13, index prefix/period]; singleBinary.replicas: 1; read/write/backend.replicas: 0}. Ablation results: schemaConfig is REQUIRED (validate.yaml refuses without it; loki.useTestSchema=true is an accepted no-persistence shortcut), zeroing read/write/backend is REQUIRED (validate.yaml: 'more than zero replicas for both single binary and simple scalable targets'), while commonConfig and singleBinary.replicas can individually be dropped for render but replication_factor:1 matters for a converging 1-instance cluster. helm install --wait exited 0; loki-0 2/2, canary, gateway, chunks-cache, results-cache all Ready in ~80s. Prerequisite: only a default StorageClass (PVC for the single binary). SHAPE 2 — object-store SimpleScalable. Minimal render: schemaConfig (object_store s3) + either (a) loki.storage.bucketNames.chunks AND .ruler plus s3 endpoint/creds (admin bucket NOT required — verified chunks+ruler alone renders), or (b) just minio.enabled=true, which auto-wires bucketNames/endpoint to the bundled MinIO. CRITICAL live-only finding: shape 2 with chart defaults renders fine but does NOT converge on a small cluster — read/write/backend default to 3 replicas each with HARD podAntiAffinity (requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution on kubernetes.io/hostname, confirmed in values.yaml), so on a single-node cluster 6 pods sit Pending forever ('didn't match pod anti-affinity rules'). Converging minimal shape 2 on one node: add read/write/backend.replicas: 1 + replication_factor: 1 (verified: all 8 pods Ready, helm --wait exit 0). Different prerequisites: shape 1 needs only a PVC; shape 2 needs an object store (bundled MinIO or external S3 with pre-created chunks+ruler buckets and credentials) AND either >=3 nodes or reduced replicas because of the default hard anti-affinity.
attempts.method: helm pull grafana/loki 7.0.0; reproduced default template failure; ablation sweep with helm template (dropped each value in turn to find the true minimum, including admin-bucket and useTestSchema probes); then two live helm install --wait runs on kind bakeoff2 (filesystem single-binary converged; SSS with defaults proved unschedulable via kubectl describe showing anti-affinity FailedScheduling; SSS with replicas=1 converged with bundled MinIO); confirmed hard anti-affinity is the chart default in values.yaml.
attempts.whatWouldChangeYourMind: A multi-day soak showing the single-binary filesystem shape failing compaction/retention with this schemaConfig, or evidence that a production S3 (not MinIO) needs additional values (region/signature settings) beyond endpoint+creds+bucketNames to converge.

attempts.answer: Yes, the render engine is the actual cause, demonstrated live. I built a chart whose ConfigMap embeds the result of lookup("v1","ConfigMap","default","seed-cm") and pre-created seed-cm (color=blue) on the cluster. Offline `helm template` (exactly what Argo CD's repo-server runs — it has no cluster access) rendered found:"no", seedValue:"<empty>": lookup() returns an empty map/nil offline, silently, with no error. A real `helm install` (what Flux's helm-controller does via the Helm SDK inside the cluster) rendered found:"yes", seedValue:"blue" — lookup() hit the live API server at install time. `helm template --dry-run=server` also resolved it (yes/blue), confirming it is purely a question of whether the renderer has an API connection. Mechanism of the symptom: Argo computes desired state from the offline render (lookup==nil branch), compares it to the live object that was actually created with the lookup-resolved values (by Flux, by helm install, or by the resource's own in-cluster mutation), sees a permanent field diff, and reports OutOfSync forever; syncing doesn't fix it because Argo's own apply writes the nil-branch version and the next comparison still differs (or an operator/controller re-mutates it). Flux is clean because helm-controller's stored release manifest was rendered against the live cluster, so its drift detection compares like with like. What offline `helm template` misses: (1) lookup() always returns empty — no error, so nil-guard branches silently activate; (2) .Capabilities.APIVersions/KubeVersion are client defaults, not the real cluster; (3) no server-side validation/defaulting; (4) hooks don't run. Fixes, in order of preference: make lookup() branches degrade to the same output when nil (idempotent default); or add an ignoreDifferences/managedFieldsManagers entry in the Argo Application for the lookup-derived fields; Argo has no supported flag to give repo-server cluster-scoped lookup.
attempts.method: Built a minimal chart calling lookup() on a seeded ConfigMap on the bakeoff2 kind cluster; compared three render paths side by side: offline helm template (Argo repo-server equivalent) vs helm template --dry-run=server vs real helm install (Flux helm-controller equivalent). Argo/Flux internal behavior (repo-server offline template, helm-controller SDK install) asserted from knowledge, not by installing the controllers.
attempts.whatWouldChangeYourMind: A full Argo CD install demonstrating repo-server resolving lookup() (e.g. a new flag/feature after my knowledge cutoff), or evidence the specific fleet chart's OutOfSync diff is in fields unrelated to any lookup() branch.

attempts.answer: On a first install via plain `kubectl apply` of an OCI-pulled rendered bundle, the CR does NOT get created — and there are two distinct failure layers, both shown live. Layer 1: `helm template` by DEFAULT omits the crds/ directory entirely (verified: 0 CustomResourceDefinition docs without --include-crds, 1 with it), so unless the bundle was rendered with --include-crds the CRD itself never ships and the CR fails with 'no matches for kind'. Layer 2: even with --include-crds, where the CRD is first in the file, a single `kubectl apply -f bundle.yaml` on a fresh cluster fails — verified live on kind: 'customresourcedefinition widgets.example.com created' followed immediately by 'error: resource mapping not found for name: demo-widget ... no matches for kind Widget in version example.com/v1 — ensure CRDs are installed first' (kubectl's discovery/REST-mapping is built before the just-created CRD is served/established). An immediate second apply succeeded (CRD unchanged, CR created). Path-by-path: helm install — CORRECT, verified live: it installs crds/ before templates and waits for establishment; first-pass install created both CRD and CR. Argo CD — correct in practice: it renders with --include-crds and its sync orders CRDs at the top of its kind-priority list, waits for them, and its retry loop covers the establishment race. Flux — correct on both paths: helm-controller performs a real helm install (crds/ policy default Create), and kustomize-controller's server-side apply stages CRDs+namespaces first and waits for Established before applying dependents. Plain kubectl apply — the broken one. Minimal fix (two requirements): (1) render the bundle with `helm template --include-crds`; (2) split the apply into two passes with an establishment wait: `kubectl apply -f crds.yaml && kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd --all --timeout=60s && kubectl apply -f bundle.yaml`. The absolute-minimum crude fix is simply applying the (--include-crds) bundle twice — verified the second pass succeeds — but the wait-based two-pass is the deterministic version.
attempts.method: Built a minimal chart with crds/widget-crd.yaml + templates/cr.yaml; compared helm template with/without --include-crds; on fresh kind cluster bakeoff2 ran single-pass kubectl apply (failed on CR), immediate re-apply (succeeded), then deleted the CRD and ran helm install first-pass (succeeded, CR present). Argo CD and Flux ordering behavior asserted from knowledge of their sync/apply implementations, not tested live within budget.
attempts.whatWouldChangeYourMind: For the kubectl-apply and helm-install halves nothing short of a contradicting rerun — both were observed directly. For the Argo/Flux halves: a live first-sync test on the fleet's actual Argo/Flux versions showing a CRD-establishment race their retry/wait logic doesn't cover (e.g. very large CRDs with conversion webhooks).

attempts.answer: YES, Fairwinds genuinely republished different bytes under version 10.3.0, and it was almost certainly benign CI churn, not tampering. Evidence: (1) Live pull today gives sha256:3e51ce8032b0217d667b7e9084d36c76262b4ea566151f8fa47d422cbbd475db, matching both charts.fairwinds.com/stable/index.yaml and Artifact Hub. (2) The 10.3.0 chart source landed 2026-02-24 (FairwindsOps/charts commit 711b1723, PR #1746), but the index entry's created stamp is 2026-06-11T14:11:33Z — the tarball was re-packaged ~3.5 months after release. (3) Root cause is public: until commit de0af54f (2026-07-14, PR #1907, titled 'Avoid trigger artifact hub re-release on chart release'), scripts/sync.sh re-ran `helm dependency build` + `helm package` on every chart's CURRENT version on EVERY master build and `aws s3 sync`'d the result over the bucket copy — so 10.3.0 was overwritten repeatedly from Feb 24 until 10.4.0 superseded it on Jun 11 18:08Z. The final repack (14:11:33Z) ran 2 minutes after commit 6f52b95a 'Update CircleCI major updates to v15' (14:09Z) — a CI-environment change immediately preceding the byte change (helm itself was pinned at 3.16.1 throughout; helm package is deterministic for identical input, which I verified locally, so some packaging-environment or vendored input changed). WERE THE ORIGINAL BYTES REAL? Almost certainly yes — sha256:9498a6f49cde... was an earlier build of the same commit from the same official pipeline; this repo republished as routine behavior, so an earlier different digest is exactly what that pipeline produces. However, no public record of that exact digest survives (S3 object overwritten, CloudFront invalidated, Artifact Hub stores only the latest digest per version, no Wayback captures of the index in 2026), so I cannot cryptographically confirm 9498a6f4 was ever served — only that the mechanism guarantees earlier different digests existed. WHAT IS INSIDE NOW vs WHAT YOU REVIEWED: I diffed the current tarball against git at 711b1723 — the goldilocks templates/ and values.yaml are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the Feb source (only Chart.yaml is re-serialized by helm package, semantically identical), and the vendored dependencies are vpa 4.8.1 + metrics-server 3.13.0 exactly as pinned in the committed Chart.lock (generated 2025-08-19). The exact byte-diff against your vetted tarball is unrecoverable, but since no commit touched stable/goldilocks between Feb 24 and Jun 11, the delta is confined to packaging metadata and possibly re-fetched dependency bytes — the chart logic you reviewed is unchanged. Recommendation: re-pin to 3e51ce... after confirming the tarball matches git (I did; it does), and treat Fairwinds digests before 2026-07-14 as unstable.
attempts.method: helm pull + shasum for live digest; parsed charts.fairwinds.com/stable/index.yaml created/digest fields for all versions; Artifact Hub API for its recorded digest; GitHub API (gh) for FairwindsOps/charts commit history of stable/goldilocks and scripts/sync.sh (found the Jul-14 anti-republish guard commit and the Jun-11 CircleCI-update commit 2 min before the final repack); extracted the tarball and diffed templates/values against git commit 711b1723 (identical); read Chart.lock and vendored subchart versions; tested helm package determinism locally; probed S3 list-object-versions (403) and Wayback CDX (no captures) for the old bytes.
attempts.whatWouldChangeYourMind: Any surviving artifact of the 9498a6f4 tarball (a cached copy in one of your environments, a proxy cache, or an S3 version listing) whose content diverges from git commit 711b1723 — that would convert this from CI churn into a supply-chain incident. Staking production applies to 'republish happened, current bytes match audited source'; I would NOT stake production on any claim about the exact contents of the old tarball.

attempts.answer: CANNOT-DETERMINE as posed, for two independent reasons. (1) I do not have your 139-chart dependency inventory — it lives in the helm-expt repo this control arm is barred from reading, so I cannot enumerate which publishers are even in scope. (2) Even with the list, the 'both digests' requirement is unrecoverable from public data for most republish cases: repos hosted on plain buckets/CDNs (Fairwinds S3+CloudFront) and OCI registries overwrite in place — the superseded digest exists afterward only in consumers' own pull logs, lockfiles, or caches. What IS publicly determinable, and how: (a) CONFIRMED systemic republisher this year: Fairwinds (charts.fairwinds.com) — until 2026-07-14 (PR #1907) its CI re-packaged and re-uploaded the current version of EVERY chart in the repo on every master build, so any Fairwinds chart version that was 'current' across multiple builds was served under multiple digests with an unchanged version string; goldilocks 10.3.0 (final digest 3e51ce8032b0..., last repack 2026-06-11T14:11:33Z) is the verified example, and fairwinds-insights 9.3.2/9.4.0/9.5.0 carry same-window rebuild stamps. Audit window for Fairwinds pulls: anything pulled before 2026-07-14 should be re-verified against today's index. (b) For publishers whose index.yaml lives in git (GitHub Pages repos: prometheus-community, grafana, chart-releaser-based repos generally), the complete digest history per version IS recoverable — `git log -p index.yaml` on the gh-pages branch shows every digest a version ever had; a republish appears as a modified digest line for an existing version. That is the query to run per publisher once you have the inventory. (c) Heuristic red flag without git history: an index entry whose 'created' timestamp postdates the version's source-commit/release date (that is exactly how goldilocks 10.3.0 was caught). Fabricating a completed 139-row list with paired digests would be dishonest; the honest deliverable is the Fairwinds finding plus the per-hosting-type recovery method above, joined against your own recorded pins.

attempts.answer: Safe step for your objects: between kube-prometheus-stack 85.3.3 and 86.1.0 (prometheus-operator CRDs 0.90.1 -> 0.91.0), the same 10 CRDs exist on both sides — none added, none removed — every CRD remains single-version (alertmanagers/prometheuses/prometheusrules/servicemonitors/podmonitors/probes/thanosrulers at v1; alertmanagerconfigs/prometheusagents/scrapeconfigs at v1alpha1), and NO served or storage flags flip anywhere. All schema changes are purely ADDITIVE property paths: AlertmanagerConfig v1alpha1 gains .spec.receivers[].emailConfigs[].threading (+.threadByDate) and .spec.receivers[].snsConfigs[].sigv4.externalId; Alertmanager v1 gains .spec.alertmanagerConfiguration.global.mattermost.webhookURL{key,name,optional}; PrometheusAgent v1alpha1 gains .spec.remoteWrite[].sigv4.externalId and .spec.shardingStrategy{mode,topology{externalLabelName,values}}; Prometheus v1 gains .spec.alerting.alertmanagers[].sigv4.externalId, .spec.remoteWrite[].sigv4.externalId, .spec.shardingStrategy{...}, .spec.thanos.grpcServerTlsConfig.{cipherSuites,curves}; ScrapeConfig v1alpha1 gains .spec.consulSDConfigs[].healthFilter; ThanosRuler v1 gains .spec.grpcServerTlsConfig.{cipherSuites,curves} and .spec.remoteWrite[].sigv4.externalId. PrometheusRule, ServiceMonitor, PodMonitor, and Probe schemas are BYTE-IDENTICAL except the operator.prometheus.io/version annotation. Consequence: your existing PrometheusRule and AlertmanagerConfig objects cannot start failing validation — their schemas only gained optional fields (PrometheusRule's didn't change at all). One operational caveat: kps ships CRDs in the 'crds' subchart's crds/ directory, which Helm applies on install but does NOT upgrade — apply the 86.1.0 CRD files manually (kubectl apply --server-side) before/with the chart upgrade, or the new optional fields simply won't exist yet (harmless to old objects either way).
attempts.method: helm pull of both chart versions from prometheus-community; extracted charts/crds/crds/*.yaml; wrote a Python semantic differ that compares each CRD's versions[] (name/served/storage) and recursively enumerates every openAPIV3Schema property path (including items[] and additionalProperties{}), reporting added/removed paths per version plus a full-schema text comparison to catch validation-only changes.
attempts.whatWouldChangeYourMind: A discrepancy between the chart-shipped CRDs and what the 0.91.0 operator itself expects at runtime, or evidence the cluster's installed CRDs were already drifted from 85.3.3's shipped copies (check with kubectl diff against the 85.3.3 files first).

attempts.answer: With default values, the 85.3.3 -> 87.19.2 jump renders NO destructive changes: I templated both versions (helm template, namespace monitoring, kube-version 1.33) and diffed the full object inventories. Results: (1) Renames/orphans: zero objects present in 85.3.3 and absent in 87.19.2; the only inventory change is one NEW ConfigMap (kps-kube-prometheus-stack-k8s-resources-nodes-overview, a Grafana dashboard). Same names for every Deployment, DaemonSet, Service, ServiceAccount, RBAC object, webhook, and CR. (2) Immutable selectors: spec.selector is unchanged on every common Deployment and DaemonSet (operator, grafana, kube-state-metrics, prometheus-node-exporter) — no 'field is immutable' failures, no delete-and-recreate needed. (3) StatefulSets: the chart renders none directly (prometheus-operator creates them from the Prometheus/Alertmanager CRs); the CR spec diff is ONLY image/version bumps (prometheus v3.11.3-distroless -> v3.13.1-distroless, alertmanager v0.32.1 -> v0.33.1), which the operator handles as a rolling pod update — no selector, serviceName, shard, or storage/volumeClaimTemplate-affecting fields change, so the operator will not recreate the StatefulSets or detach PVCs. (4) Service identity: no Service changes type, clusterIP, selector, or ports. The remaining 121 common objects differ only in labels/annotations (chart version, app.kubernetes.io/version) and dashboard/rule content — all patchable in place. IMPORTANT SCOPE CAVEATS: this verdict is for DEFAULT values; re-run the same render-diff with your production values files before trusting it (features you enable — thanosRuler, ingresses, additional scrape configs, grafana persistence — bring objects my render never produced). Also apply the 87.19.2 CRDs manually before upgrading (helm won't), and note the operator itself jumps 0.90.1 -> 0.96.x-era behavior, so pod templates inside the operator-managed StatefulSets will roll even though nothing is destructive. Command to reproduce with your values: helm template each version with identical release name/namespace/values, then diff kind/name inventory plus spec.selector, volumeClaimTemplates, serviceName, and Service type/clusterIP/selector/ports.
attempts.method: Pulled both chart versions, rendered with helm template (identical release name/namespace, --kube-version 1.33.0, default values), parsed both streams with Python, and diffed: (kind,namespace,name) inventory for orphans/renames; spec.selector on all Deployments/DaemonSets/StatefulSets; volumeClaimTemplates+serviceName on StatefulSets; type/clusterIP/selector/ports on Services; unified-diff of the Prometheus and Alertmanager CR specs to catch operator-side StatefulSet-recreation triggers.
attempts.whatWouldChangeYourMind: Running the identical render-diff with the actual production values files (and the real release name, since kps derives object names from it) — default-values cleanliness does not cover chart paths my render never exercised; I would stake production only after that values-accurate diff also comes back clean.
